DMHS is a very competitive and robust architecture, that can be trained end-to-end on multiple data sources.

the DMHS architecture is able to learn a complete and integrated model for the 2d-3d human sensing problem, by means of a unified training protocol, and that this model can be trained to state-of-the-art performance levels.

our DMHS system is a strong baseline for future research in monocular 2d-3d human sensing, and that the multitask approach is a viable and efficient way of learning and integrating multiple tasks in a single deep model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present a unified framework for human sensing, that is able to achieve state-of-the-art accuracy in both 2d and in 3d, while being able to work on monocular RGB images only.
we present the first fully automatic system that can robustly estimate 2d and/or 3d pose from a single monocular image.

we present a novel multitask architecture that allows for the training of a deep model with multiple datasets, each of them with a limited scope, and demonstrate that the system achieves state-of-the-art performance in both 2d and in 3d human analysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that

deep learning models for human sensing can be trained in a unified fashion, with multiple datasets and multiple tasks, and that this approach leads to a significant performance gain over single-task models trained in isolation.
a single, unified, deep model can achieve state-of-the-art performance for 2d and for 3d human pose estimation, and can be trained with limited training data.
deep multitask learning allows us to build complex models for human sensing by taking advantage of the available data, even if it is incomplete or limited.
